study type: Cross-sectional instrument evaluation design with an embedded between-subjects design
outcome: Psychometric properties of the Italian Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised (I-BSS-R) (factor structure, validity, reliability, internal consistency)
Birth satisfaction scores (I-BSS-R sub-scales and total scores)
Stress experienced during childbearing sub-scale scores (I-BSS-R SE)
cohort: 297 women who had recently given birth provided data for analysis.
finding: The Italian version of the BSS-R (I-BSS-R) was found to be a valid translation with good psychometric properties, except for internal consistency, and women who attended antenatal classes had significantly lower stress experienced during childbearing.
